reason: Both satisfy all hard requirements equally well, but Response B adds more operationally useful specifics: distinguishing WAL/temp volume fill from the main data volume, snapshotting to a separate target when the near-full disk can't host the snapshot itself, throttling writes as a stopgap if the disk will fill before the snapshot completes, and concrete post-mitigation data-integrity validation (checksums/row counts, replica consistency) rather than a vaguer check.
